chunks: What! Do the (unbelievers) expect that the angels should descend, or the sentence of your Lord come to pass? So had the people done before them; yet God did not wrong them, they wronged themselves.

key_terms.أَمْرُ رَبِّهِمْ: The command/decreed matter of their Lord

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about how God treats those who wrong themselves?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah An-Nahl underscores the concept of 'self-inflicted punishment' (azab al-nafs), illustrating that divine retribution is a natural consequence of human disbelief rather than arbitrary divine caprice. It connects the current disbelievers' impatience for the Hour with the historical precedent of earlier nations, reinforcing the Shia understanding of God's justice (Adl) where the burden of error lies with the disbelievers themselves.
